back_translation: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Son of man, pose a riddle and speak a parable to the house of Israel,
and say, the Lord GOD says this: A great eagle with great wings, long pinions, and full plumage of many colors came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
It plucked off the topmost shoot of the tree, carried it to the land of merchants, and planted it in a city of traders.
Then it took some of the seed of the land and planted it in fertile soil, set it by abundant waters, and planted it like a willow.
It sprouted and became a low, spreading vine; its branches turned toward the eagle, and its roots stayed beneath it. So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.

But there was another great eagle with great wings and much plumage, and behold, this vine turned its roots toward that eagle and stretched out its branches to it from the bed where it was planted, so that the eagle might water it.
It had been planted in good soil by abundant waters, to produce branches, bear fruit, and become a splendid vine.”

Say, the Lord GOD says this: ‘Will that vine flourish? Will it not be uprooted, its fruit stripped off, and left to wither? All its young leaves will wither, and it will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots.
Behold, even if it is transplanted, will it flourish? When the east wind strikes it, will it not wither completely? It will wither on the bed where it sprouted.’”
Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
“Say to that rebellious house, ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them, ‘Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and officials, and brought them with him to Babylon.
He took a member of the royal family, made a covenant with him, put him under oath, and carried away the leading men of the land,
so that the kingdom would be brought low and unable to lift itself up, surviving only by keeping the king of Babylon's covenant.

But that king rebelled against Babylon by sending his envoys to Egypt to ask for horses and a great army. Will he flourish? Will the one who does these things escape? Can he break a covenant and escape?
As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who enthroned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and vast horde will not help him in battle, when ramps are raised and siege walls built to destroy many lives.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant; behold, he had given his pledge, yet did all these things—he will not escape.’
Therefore the Lord GOD says this: ‘As surely as I live, I will bring down upon his head My oath that he despised and My covenant that he broke.
I will spread My net over him, and he will be caught in My snare; I will bring him to Babylon and judge him there for the treachery he committed against Me.
All his choice troops will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.
The Lord GOD says this: ‘I Myself will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar and plant it; I will pluck a tender sprig from its topmost shoots and plant it on a high, towering mountain.

I will plant it on the high mountain of Israel; it will produce branches, bear fruit, and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it and take shelter in the shade of its branches.

Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD: I bring the tall tree low and make the low tree tall; I dry up the green tree and make the withered tree bud. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I have done it.’”
